I am an **Associate Professor** in the Franklin L. Burns School of Real Estate
and Construction Management, part of the Daniels College of Business at the
**University of Denver**. My research applies the tools of applied
microeconomics to **real estate finance, sustainability, and urban economics** —
including real estate market cycles and investment, sustainable and regenerative
development in the built environment, and the economics of housing affordability.

I hold a Ph.D. in Economics from Colorado State University and an M.S. in Real
Estate and Construction Management from the University of Denver, and I bring two
decades of industry experience in real estate research, development, and
investment to my academic work.

## Research interests

- Real estate finance, investment, and market cycles
- Sustainability and regenerative development in the built environment
- Affordable housing and housing-market dynamics
- Urban, regional, and environmental economics
- Spatial econometrics and applied microeconomics

## News

- **2024** — Chaired the inaugural American Real Estate Society (ARES) Fall
  Research Symposium.
- **2023** — Published *Investable Real Estate Allocations in a Mixed-Asset
  Portfolio* (*Journal of Real Estate Portfolio Management*) and *Spatial Models
  of Travel Behavior and Land Use Restriction* (*Journal of Sustainable Real
  Estate*).
- **2022** — Promoted to Associate Professor; awarded the ARES Manuscript Prize
  for Best Real Estate Cycles paper.
